The towns of the monarchy are not starving this winter, and the army in Italy is fed. The strikes of January did not become the revolution that some had feared. A winter without hunger may postpone a collapse, and it may leave the causes of the collapse where they were. What actually happened: Austro-Hungarian forces occupied parts of Ukraine from February 1918, after the treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Ukrainian People's Republic, and Odessa was taken by Austro-Hungarian troops in the spring. The grain that came out was far less than had been promised, and the monarchy was hungry in the summer. The Ukrainian grain that the monarchy was promised under the treaty of February 1918 was a small part of what the cities needed, and the hunger of that summer was one of the causes of the strikes and the mutinies that followed.
